data.title: feat(hepta-agentd): read exact durable Objective admission through owner
data.body:
## Problem

A RunStart publication can be durable before later runtime admission fails. Current RunStatus is only an in-memory projection, so its absence or a generic submission error cannot resolve the original publication fact.

## Change

Add the narrow schema-2 ObjectiveAdmission read method to the original Agentd owner. It matches the exact saved authentication, including the original signature, canonical body, run and profile, and optionally checks a previously retained sequence/chain anchor against the recovered journal prefix. Published metadata and finite unknown reasons preserve the distinction between publication, current runtime admission and effects.

The query uses the original owner mutex and recovered journal. It does not append, recover/truncate a file, advance replay state, start an old run, reconcile effects or grant authority. Expired/revoked historical requests can still match their old publication; fresh submissions retain the original current authorization checks. Current endpoint identity and the original request generation remain separate.

17 files, +798/-2; no Cargo manifest/lock or Bazel lock changes. Original f8 and the R8 source contract remain unchanged. Desktop consumer: TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop#193.

## Executed validation

- Protocol/ledger --lib suites: 134 passed / 1 existing ignored at ee0a2e5eee299fc0f272c3ceb09ef70f2cbfaf73.
- Agentd --lib suite: 173 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored at d1d40f64eadd0210f5f6abc003cd479a0e1ee010, including four new history tests. These are two differently pinned runs, not a final-head full-suite run. Their dev-dependency graph unified default/production-cognitive-write despite no-default command flags.
- Final scoped just fix and just fmt --base f8 completed. The final change after d1 boxes Published metadata and reformats documentation without changing JSON wire; unrelated existing automatic fixes were reverted.
- Final native05 build at this exact 2be5fc052ae7b2e9fb08c68a3ae7e5a218ad37d5 head passed on x86_64 Linux with Rust 1.95.0, locked/offline dev-small, j1. Actual Agentd lib/bin rustc features=[]. Executed ELF SHA-256: a8f8aefa2199a2e41c22b8251145f064e3af767ff5357475ddb527beb86761cb.
- Actual original Fleet/Supervisor + three real desktop CLIs + newly built history probe passed 15 checks, 13 history queries, five distinct Objective requests, four durable publications, three controlled restarts and zero recovery resubmissions. Runtime report SHA-256: edbfff169707cd2946a549f9edeaf0548eefbb6765e757e7039dabf0fe430f4b. Two independent read-only reviews verified sources, five ELF identities, saved request/output bytes and journal prefixes.

## Scope and review boundaries

The actual fourth request returned submit_unknown / objective_owner_request_rejected while exact history found compiled publication #4 and RunStatus was null. Capacity exhaustion is a fixed-source/precondition inference; its specific original error bytes were not captured.

Lost reply is exercised by an original-protocol qualification harness, not by the hepta-submit CLI itself. Rollback and truncation are injected only after a confirmed controlled stop; this is not a mid-write crash or power-loss qualification. The caller-retained anchor and journal can still be jointly rolled back outside this profile.

No production issuer, model turn, Operations K/D, device effect, historical run resume, kernel G1/G2 or mobile qualification is claimed. Original failed build attempts and targeted cache-repair evidence are retained. The final native/runtime used an existing repaired cache, not a cold-build resource profile.

CI required and Architecture required, plus the consumer's new ARM64 history job, remain separate remote gates; local x86_64 success does not replace them. A separate documentation/evidence delivery preserves this code head and will be linked here.

## Published evidence

[Complete source-bound report](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/24b5c127a5c4bfb2747369526995c133de18543b/results/integration/2026-10-18-objective-history/README.md) and TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop#194 contain the actual receipts, failures, independent reviews, 11-module documentation audit and the exact reconstructible raw archive. The documentation/evidence is a separate commit with tree 8debd197581f875f9b3c86180fb808b2d8cf411d; it does not change or requalify this code head.

data.title: feat(hepta): add owner-backed Objective history and fault qualification
data.body:
## Problem

A known Objective can already have a durable original-owner publication while its submission result is unknown or current RunStatus is absent. The desktop needs an exact, bounded history query to display that fact without treating missing state as a safe retry.

## Change

Add the Linux-only, default-off objective-history feature and standalone hepta-history CLI. The caller supplies the saved exact original envelope, trusted current endpoint/AgentId/spawn/UID/PID and an optional previously retained anchor. The client checks the private Unix endpoint, SO_PEERCRED UID/PID, strict identity and metadata, one bounded frame plus EOF, whole-exchange timeout and finite outcomes. It exposes no submit, retry, generic RPC or effect method.

The original owner extension is independently pinned to TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci#2815 at 2be5fc052ae7b2e9fb08c68a3ae7e5a218ad37d5 through OBJECTIVE_HISTORY_CONTRACT.json. Original f8/R8 contracts remain unchanged. No dependency or lock changes.

Add a real original-owner history fault probe, detailed development/protocol/run documentation and an independent ARM64 history CI workflow. The G1 CPU-owner seam document is a fixed-source audit only; there is no kernel edit/build/runtime in this PR. Root README remains zero bytes.

## Executed validation

- 51 hepta-os tests, strict all-target Clippy, default-off check, fmt and all three real CLI builds passed at c080896189b6d5c1e411a28b7614c8fcdc33b188. The 12 actual compiled inputs remain byte-identical in this head.
- 22 synthetic receipt/source-contract checks passed; these are reported separately from native runtime.
- Actual actionlint 1.7.12, YAML, 12 Bash blocks and eight Python blocks passed. No shellcheck or pyflakes execution is claimed.
- Real x86_64 Linux qualification used desktop 207ff9da7dac83c57b0cbae46c4b03ecfba3baa9, the same tree 8d5de807c41090e3d987764daec9c235ebd022a1 published as this 46dcb2d691827f7aa3ad7903dae09d39fd338126 head, and final original owner 2be. The runner newly built the history probe and executed the independently preserved native05 Agentd ELF plus actual observe/submit/history CLIs.
- 15 checks / 13 history queries / five distinct Objective requests / four durable publications / three controlled restarts / zero recovery resubmissions passed. Runtime report SHA-256: edbfff169707cd2946a549f9edeaf0548eefbb6765e757e7039dabf0fe430f4b.
- Two independent read-only reviews matched 38 raw records, frozen owner/probe/CLI inputs, five ELF identities, original request/output bytes and exact rollback/truncation recovery prefixes.

## Observed behavior and remaining scope

An actual CLI generic rejection with RunStatus null still yielded exact compiled publication #4. CapacityExceeded is inferred from fixed source and two already admitted runs; the specific original error bytes were not observed. Real expiry and issuer revocation do not erase historical publication, while a distinct revoked new request is rejected without journal append.

The lost-reply case uses the original-protocol harness, not a hepta-submit CLI lost-reply execution. Storage fault injection follows confirmed controlled stop; this does not qualify abrupt crash/power loss. Query reads the original owner's recovered in-memory prefix; it does not prove current disk integrity or detect caller-anchor co-rollback.

Production issuer/request/anchor persistence, new Session/Shell history projection, Operations effect reconciliation and K↔D, final-use authority, kernel G1/G2 and mobile/device control remain separate work. Local x86_64 PASS and R8 CI do not qualify this new ARM64 workflow. A separate docs/results delivery records full evidence and the 11-module documentation audit without changing this code head.

## Published evidence

[Complete source-bound report](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/24b5c127a5c4bfb2747369526995c133de18543b/results/integration/2026-10-18-objective-history/README.md) and TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop#194 contain the actual receipts, failures, independent reviews, 11-module documentation audit and the exact reconstructible raw archive. The documentation/evidence is a separate commit with tree 8debd197581f875f9b3c86180fb808b2d8cf411d; it does not change or requalify this code head.

## Final-head transport CI evidence

The exact desktop head `46dcb2d691827f7aa3ad7903dae09d39fd338126` completed the transport job on 2026-10-18 at 10:48:42 UTC: 51 Rust tests, 22 synthetic receipt/source checks, strict Clippy, default-off check and formatting passed. The downloaded original ZIP and independent review bind all 29 source hashes to that commit. [Published CI evidence](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/1461afab03305d8b2d404b3c1d9849eac5bea6d5/results/integration/2026-10-18-objective-history-ci/README.md).

The separate original-owner-history ARM64 job remains a distinct runtime qualification; this transport result does not establish its outcome.

data.title: docs: publish R9 native history evidence and module audit
data.body:
## Outcome

Publish the complete R9 local qualification and documentation audit after the original owner build and real Objective history run passed. This is stacked on #193 so its already qualified code head remains unchanged. After #193 merges, retarget this delivery to main for a normal documentation/evidence merge.

## Included

- Actual final owner 2be native05 build and original Fleet/Supervisor runtime: 15 checks, 13 history queries, five distinct Objective requests, four durable publications, three controlled restarts, zero recovery resubmissions.
- Two independent runtime reviews, original input/output and journal-prefix evidence, five ELF identities, source/contract/lock bindings, and earlier failed build/cache-repair attempts.
- The 11-module development/technical documentation audit. All modules have concrete entry points; A04's three detailed handbooks remain only in fixed Draft #8, outside the reviewed tree. Shared ABI/build/architecture documentation is identified explicitly.
- Updated STATUS, INDEX/A07 and S2 implementation guidance. Publication, current run admission and effects remain separate. G1 is source audit only; production issuer, effect reconciliation, G1/G2 and mobile qualification remain incomplete.
- 321 original materials plus 20 primary receipts/reviews. The original tar.xz is preserved byte-for-byte as 16 ordered parts after the full blob request failed in transport; all part Git blob SHAs matched remote upload results, and actual reconstruction matched the full 24,308,524-byte SHA-256 4f8ae8d38933ff594d1e3c84db30f8a9efe2457276f08d1ea84ab4e1e85c2e4f.
- Post-archive publication/auto-merge snapshots, the transfer receipt and a complete artifact manifest.

## Validation and source identity

50 files changed, all under docs/ and results/. The 12 client compiled inputs, eight probe inputs and history contract are unchanged from execution source 207ff9da7dac83c57b0cbae46c4b03ecfba3baa9 / tree 8d5de807c41090e3d987764daec9c235ebd022a1, published as #193 head 46dcb2d691827f7aa3ad7903dae09d39fd338126.

Local delivery commit be44a8c4e76fe90b72f07ca153df8339b4696d7e and this remote delivery commit share exact tree 8debd197581f875f9b3c86180fb808b2d8cf411d. Final delivery checks validated 202 local link targets, JSON, archive reconstruction and source bindings. Root README remains zero bytes; original f8 and final owner checkouts remain clean. This docs-only finalization did not rerun Rust or the runtime.

Scoped owner test attribution remains 134 passed / 1 existing ignored at ee0 and 173 passed at d1; these are not a final-head full-suite 307 run. Desktop 51 tests remain attributed to c080 with exact compiled-input reuse. Final native/runtime evidence separately binds owner 2be.

## Current remote gates

The saved observation is 10:38:28–10:39:34 UTC, not a timeless success claim. Both source PRs were Ready/open; owner #2815 had normal auto-merge enabled with the repository-selected squash method and required aggregates still pending. Desktop's old fixed-f8 ARM64 job succeeded, while the new history ARM64 job had not yet been generated. Local x86_64 PASS and prior f8 CI do not qualify the new ARM64 history workflow.

The real lost-reply case is an original-protocol harness; faults are injected after controlled stop. Specific CapacityExceeded error bytes were not observed. Those qualifications remain explicit in the report.

Entry point: results/integration/2026-10-18-objective-history/README.md.

## Final-head transport CI evidence

The exact desktop head `46dcb2d691827f7aa3ad7903dae09d39fd338126` completed the transport job on 2026-10-18 at 10:48:42 UTC: 51 Rust tests, 22 synthetic receipt/source checks, strict Clippy, default-off check and formatting passed. The downloaded original ZIP and independent review bind all 29 source hashes to that commit. [Published CI evidence](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/1461afab03305d8b2d404b3c1d9849eac5bea6d5/results/integration/2026-10-18-objective-history-ci/README.md).

The separate original-owner-history ARM64 job remains a distinct runtime qualification; this transport result does not establish its outcome.
